paper_id: One-Shot Sequential Federated Learning for Non-IID Data by Enhancing Local Model Diversity
title: One-Shot Sequential Federated Learning for Non-IID Data by Enhancing Local Model Diversity
motivation: SFL reduces communication rounds but struggles with non-IID data; one-shot SFL with single client communication is underexplored and suffers from insufficient diversity.
problem_framing: One-shot SFL problem: each client receives one model from adjacent client, limited info exchange, non-IID data causes divergence from global optimum.
key_insight: Local model pool with diverse starting points enables knowledge transfer across clients; averaging diverse models improves generalization beyond single-trajectory training.
method_signature: FedELMY: model pool per client, initialize new model as average of pool, distance regularization d1 (diversify) + d2 (prevent divergence).
evaluation_criteria: Test accuracy on CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet, PACS, Office-Caltech-10 under label-skew and domain-shift non-IID partitions.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Higher computation cost: each client trains S models instead of 1 model; simply increasing local epochs causes overfitting.
evidence_for_taste: Our insight is to utilize the diversity of models
directly applying such a diversity strategy in SFL is not feasible
directly increasing local epochs does not always improve model performance
overfitting due to excessive local training
model number S grew to around 10, the performance started to become stable
thinking_moves: 把one-shot SFL的communication限制重新定义成diversity利用问题
借用SWAD的经验：相似训练loss但不同参数的模型ensemble可以提升泛化
用两个对立的distance term平衡探索与收敛稳定性
通过ablation验证diversity本身已优于baseline，再加regularization进一步提升
